subject: physical-education
title: Launch and diagnostic: space and body control
essential_question: How can understanding movement foundations and safe participation help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?
learning_objectives: Activate prior knowledge about space and body control, surface initial thinking without penalty, and establish the unit question.
Use subject-appropriate evidence or representation to communicate understanding of space and body control.
Check, revise, or improve work about space and body control using stated success criteria.
success_criteria: The learner completes the central task about space and body control.
The learner gives evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can identify a next step.
materials: unit-specific source, model, manipulatives, safe materials, or approved digital tool

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Present a brief, accessible prompt connected to “space and body control.” Ask the learner to notice, predict, estimate, recall, or pose a question before instruction.

Prepare the body, demonstrate the skill, practice at adjustable challenge levels, use safe feedback, and cool down with reflection. Keep the explanation centered on space and body control. Name the success criteria and model how to check work or evidence.
Complete two supported examples or source-based tasks about space and body control. After each step, ask: “What evidence or reasoning supports that move?” Fade prompts on the second example.
Learner completes a new application of space and body control and records both the result and the reasoning, evidence, process, or design choice that produced it.
In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about space and body control; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim.

student_activity: Learner completes a new application of space and body control and records both the result and the reasoning, evidence, process, or design choice that produced it.
formative_check: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about space and body control; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score the stated learning target, accuracy, evidence/reasoning, and revision. Accept multiple valid approaches when they meet the criteria. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for space and body control, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item.
Ask the learner to explain or represent why the process for space and body control works before continuing.
Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of space and body control, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review.
Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking space and body control mastered.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one answer. Use safe participation, skill cues, personal progress, strategy use, and self-assessment without body-size scoring; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two occasions when feasible.
extension: Apply space and body control under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language.
Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Check space, footwear, surface, weather, and equipment before movement.
Stop for pain, dizziness, breathing difficulty, head impact, or unsafe conditions and tell an adult.
Score skill, strategy, consistency, and reflection—not body size, weight, speed alone, or comparison with others.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, map, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting space and body control.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile/concrete model, or teacher demonstration.

parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. Do not expose raw private reflections, raw answers, voice recordings, or diagnosis language. For safety-critical tasks, record only the needed guardian confirmation.
home_connection: Invite the learner to notice one safe, optional example of space and body control in daily life. No purchase, account creation, photograph, or private disclosure is required.

essential_question: How can understanding personal activity portfolio and celebration help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?
learning_objectives: Practice skill transfer with prompts, feedback, and gradually reduced support.
Use subject-appropriate evidence or representation to communicate understanding of skill transfer.
Check, revise, or improve work about skill transfer using stated success criteria.
success_criteria: The learner completes the central task about skill transfer.
The learner gives evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can identify a next step.
materials: unit-specific source, model, manipulatives, safe materials, or approved digital tool

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Present a brief, accessible prompt connected to “skill transfer.” Ask the learner to notice, predict, estimate, recall, or pose a question before instruction.

Prepare the body, demonstrate the skill, practice at adjustable challenge levels, use safe feedback, and cool down with reflection. Keep the explanation centered on skill transfer. Name the success criteria and model how to check work or evidence.
Complete two supported examples or source-based tasks about skill transfer. After each step, ask: “What evidence or reasoning supports that move?” Fade prompts on the second example.
Learner completes a new application of skill transfer and records both the result and the reasoning, evidence, process, or design choice that produced it.
In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about skill transfer; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim.

student_activity: Learner completes a new application of skill transfer and records both the result and the reasoning, evidence, process, or design choice that produced it.
formative_check: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about skill transfer; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score the stated learning target, accuracy, evidence/reasoning, and revision. Accept multiple valid approaches when they meet the criteria. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for skill transfer, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item.
Ask the learner to explain or represent why the process for skill transfer works before continuing.
Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of skill transfer, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review.
Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking skill transfer mastered.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one answer. Use safe participation, skill cues, personal progress, strategy use, and self-assessment without body-size scoring; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two occasions when feasible.
extension: Apply skill transfer under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language.
Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Check space, footwear, surface, weather, and equipment before movement.
Stop for pain, dizziness, breathing difficulty, head impact, or unsafe conditions and tell an adult.
Score skill, strategy, consistency, and reflection—not body size, weight, speed alone, or comparison with others.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, map, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting skill transfer.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile/concrete model, or teacher demonstration.

parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. Do not expose raw private reflections, raw answers, voice recordings, or diagnosis language. For safety-critical tasks, record only the needed guardian confirmation.
home_connection: Invite the learner to notice one safe, optional example of skill transfer in daily life. No purchase, account creation, photograph, or private disclosure is required.
